name: Apoptosis Mechanisms, Caspase Cascades, and Cell Cycle Checkpoints
hyTerms: assembling the DISC to activate caspase-8

reference.source: Medical Biochemistry 5th ed / Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry 8th ed
clinicalPearls: Apoptosis is executed by initiator (caspase-8, -9) and executioner (caspase-3, -6, -7) cysteine proteases
Intrinsic apoptosis involves Bax/Bak pore formation, outer mitochondrial membrane permeabilization, and cytochrome c release
Cytochrome c binds Apaf-1 in the presence of dATP to form the wheel-shaped apoptosome, activating procaspase-9
Extrinsic apoptosis is initiated by FasL/TNF binding death receptors, assembling the DISC to activate caspase-8
The p53 tumor suppressor arrests cells at the G1/S checkpoint by transactivating p21 (CDKN1A), which inhibits CDK4/6
reference.pathophysiology: Programmed cell death balances cellular proliferation to maintain tissue architecture. DNA double-strand breaks activate ATM/ATR kinases that stabilize p53, upregulating pro-apoptotic Puma, Noxa, and Bax. Bax and Bak oligomerize within the outer mitochondrial membrane, releasing cytochrome c into the cytosol. Cytosolic cytochrome c recruits Apaf-1 to assemble the apoptosome, activating caspase-9 and executioner caspase-3 to cleave cellular substrates without inflammatory necrosis.
additionalDifferentials: Follicular lymphoma (t(14;18) BCL2 overexpression evading apoptosis)
Li-Fraumeni syndrome (germline TP53 loss predisposing to diverse malignancies)
additionalInvestigations: Immunohistochemistry for cleaved (active) Caspase-3 in tissue biopsy specimens
TUNEL assay (terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase dUTP nick end labeling) for DNA fragmentation
Flow cytometric Annexin V / Propidium Iodide dual staining for early apoptotic cells
TP53 gene sequencing in malignant and premalignant lesions
